## Berlin Deposit Dispute Checklist
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

You have a strong starting point if you have dated move-in/move-out photos and the claimed damage is just normal wear or unclear in cause. Keep the tone factual, ask for proof, and avoid admitting liability before you see their calculation.

## What to Gather Before You Reply
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/book.svg

- Lease agreement and any addenda
- Move-in handover protocol and move-out handover protocol, if signed
- Dated move-in photos and dated move-out photos
- Any messages with the landlord or property manager about the walls
- The landlord’s deduction notice and itemized cost breakdown
- Repair invoice, contractor quote, or calculation they used
- Proof of when the deposit was paid and the amount
- Witness notes, if someone was present at handover
- Proof that the lease ended on **2025-04-30**
- Any evidence that the wall condition was already present at move-in or is normal wear

## Practical Dispute Checklist
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/check2-square.svg

| Step | What to do | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Compare move-in and move-out photos side by side | Shows whether the condition changed during your tenancy |
| 2 | Check whether the issue is actual damage or normal wear | Landlords usually cannot charge for ordinary use |
| 3 | Ask for an itemized deduction with receipts or quotes | Prevents vague or inflated claims |
| 4 | Verify whether the claimed repair is proportional to the alleged damage | Helps challenge full-wall repainting for minor marks |
| 5 | Confirm the handover protocol wording | Signed notes can support your version of events |
| 6 | Reply in writing and keep a calm record | Creates a paper trail if the dispute escalates |
| 7 | Set a deadline for their evidence and return of the disputed amount | Pushes the issue forward without sounding hostile |

## Neutral Email Template
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/phone.svg

Subject: Request for itemized explanation of deposit deduction

Dear [Landlord/Property Manager Name],

Thank you for your message regarding the deposit deduction after the lease ended on 2025-04-30.

I dispute the deduction for alleged wall damage and would like to review the basis for it before agreeing to any amount being withheld. I have dated photos from move-in and move-out, and I would appreciate if you could send me:

- A detailed explanation of the specific damage being claimed
- The exact location(s) on the wall
- Any move-in or move-out handover notes you are relying on
- Copies of invoices, contractor quotes, or other cost calculations
- A breakdown showing how the deducted amount was calculated

Based on my records, the condition of the apartment appears consistent with normal use, or the issue may have existed before move-out. Please also confirm the amount of the deposit currently being withheld and return any undisputed portion without delay.

I would appreciate your written response by [date, e.g. 7–14 days from now].

Kind regards,
[Your full name]
[Address of the apartment]
[Phone number or email]

## How to Strengthen Your Position
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shield-check.svg

- Keep all communication in writing
- Do not say the damage is “probably my fault”
- Refer to “alleged damage” or “claimed deduction”
- If the wall issue is small, emphasize normal wear and tear
- If they provide no invoice or quote, ask again for documentation
- If the deduction seems excessive, ask for the repair scope and whether only the damaged section was addressed

## Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Download checklist] https://www.berliner-mieterverein.de/
Action: [Button: Tenant advice] https://www.mieterbund.de/
Action: [Button: Send dispute email] https://www.bmj.de/EN/Home/home_node.html

## Sources
- Berlin tenant support overview: https://www.berliner-mieterverein.de/
- German Tenants’ Association: https://www.mieterbund.de/
- Federal Ministry of Justice: https://www.bmj.de/EN/Home/home_node.html
